slot.brief: Compare rms speeds of two gases (e.g. H₂ vs O₂) at same temperature using v ∝ 1/√M; pick the ratio.

stem: At the same temperature, the ratio of the rms speed of hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) to that of oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) is:

verdicts.working: At the same temperature, rms speed is proportional to the inverse square root of molar mass. The ratio is √(32/2) = 4.

working:
$v_\text{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$.

$M(\text{H}_2) = 2$, $M(\text{O}_2) = 32$.

$\dfrac{v_{\text{H}_2}}{v_{\text{O}_2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_{\text{O}_2}}{M_{\text{H}_2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{32}{2}} = \sqrt{16} = 4$.

Independent check: At the same temperature, rms speed is proportional to the inverse square root of molar mass. The ratio is √(32/2) = 4.
solution:
At the same temperature, $v_{\rm rms}\propto 1/\sqrt{M}$. Hence, using $M_{\text{H}_2}=2$ and $M_{\text{O}_2}=32$,
$$\frac{v_{\text{H}_2}}{v_{\text{O}_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{2}}=4.$$
